decisions.issues: Minor only. A thin maroon cord, read as a sword belt, shows at the waist under the mundu folds. It is not a broad red sash. The trader's towel is on his right shoulder here and on his left in panel 1.3. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch23 row: Kerala topknot with grey at the temples, no turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud, silver chain, talwar at his left hip, cream shoulder cloth. The trader matches the script: grey beard, bare head and chest, checked lungi, towel, clay cup, talking up at Nagoji. The flag is plain white and the art has no text. Open sky at upper centre and upper right leaves room for all three balloons.

The trader does not quite match panel 1.2. Here he has short curly grey hair, a close-trimmed beard and a heavier build. In 1.2 his hair is longer and swept back, and his beard is fuller. His towel has also moved to the other shoulder. He is not a principal, he still fits the script description, and the reader can take him as the same man, so this is acceptable. The beat works: he is close, shrugs with an open palm and holds a clay cup of buttermilk. The courtyard, laterite wall and tiled verandah match 1.2. The oil lamp is clay with an open flame. Both hands are sound and there is no text. Clear sky in the upper right gives room for the long and medium balloons, away from his face and the shrugging hand.

Clean. The face matches the V13 Varma sheet: thick moustache, pearl drop earrings and gold bead necklaces. He is bare-headed with his hair in a knot above and behind his LEFT ear, with no turban, crest or crown. He is bare-chested under a cream cloth with a gold border. The border pattern is geometric, not pseudo-text. There is no bandage, which is correct because the knife wound comes later in the chapter. He shows a faint amused smirk, set in the same laterite courtyard and verandah. Open sky in the upper left takes both balloons clear of his face.

Clean on the main checks. Nagoji has a topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a small round gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it, a silver chain, a cream mundu and shoulder cloth, and no turban or sash. He rides Kayal, a bay with black points and no white markings. Padmini rides beside him in a cream sari with a gold border and no blouse, with simple gold, the thick hair coiled at the nape and the staff laid across her saddle. The column is all there: turbaned riders with tall spears on dark horses, musketeers in white on foot with long matchlocks, and a brass light gun on a carriage with bullocks, on a red dirt track. There is no text, blood or European kit, and the large clear sky upper right holds both the caption and the balloon. Minor points: Padmini's hair is more grey than 'black threaded with grey'. Her staff is a turned pole with brass bands, where her sheet shows a knobbly natural stick, so at a glance it reads a little like a musket barrel. She and Nagoji wear riding boots. The Nair musketeers wear turbans, where bare-headed topknots would be more accurate. The forearm scar is not visible. None of these is disqualifying.

Minor only. Nagoji matches: topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, no turban or red sash. He wears a sheathed sword at the hip, which is not a knife. Kayal is a bay with black points and no white markings. The covered dead wear heavy leather boots and belts that read a little soldierly, but no faces or blood show. The large clear sky at upper right takes both Ponnan balloons.

Clean. Spearmen and archers stand across the road, with matchlockmen on both slopes holding smoking slow-match at their wrists. The plain green banners carry no writing, and the raja sits on a low stool in the centre of the road. He is drawn a little larger than 'very small' but still reads as distant. Some raiders wear white head cloths. The pale sky between the slopes is clear for both captions.

Clean pick. It is a true close-up, as the r1 correction asked. Brows are lowered, the lids narrowed a fraction and the eyes cut sideways. He has long black hair swept back loose with no bun, a thick moustache, a clean chin, heavy gold ear hoops, several neck chains and a bare chest. Acceptable, and it fixes the r1 failures. There is no stool in the road and no yellow flags. The slope men are bare-chested in indigo head cloths under plain green banners, and the foreground musketman's matchlock glows correctly at the lock, not at the muzzle. His open palm is raised and his eyes are not on Ponnan. Ponnan has curly hair, a moustache, the red shoulder cloth, a short jacket and a spear, on a smaller horse. Kayal is bay with a black mane. Most r1 fixes landed. From behind, the raja's hair is long, sleek and loose with no bun. Nagoji wears the cream shoulder cloth and silver chain, and his face is right: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, clean chin and stud. The column flies a plain red flag, and the forearm mark is a faint pale scar. The composition is good: the raja's back and stool, Kayal, the Nairs and the gun on its bullock carriage, with wide sky for the balloons. Two problems rule it out. (1) Every matchlock man on both slopes, about eight guns, has an orange flash at the muzzle with smoke trailing from it. That reads as gunfire during the parley, the same failure that rejected 3.3 and 3.5 in r1. (2) Nagoji still makes an open-palm gesture out to his side toward the right slope instead of gesturing back the way they came.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly. In the left foreground: the raja's broad bare back, his long sleek black hair falling loose to the shoulders, the gold ear hoop, the gold-edged sash, the sword and the carved wooden stool. At right centre: Nagoji on Kayal, with topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear studs, the cream shoulder cloth over the white mundu and the silver chain. Behind him: the white-turbaned Nair musketeers with crossed belts and the small gun on its white-bullock carriage under a plain red flag. Keep the plain green banners and the matchlock men on both slopes, and the open sky at top centre. Fix two things. First, no gun is being fired. Every matchlock on the slopes is held aimed but silent, with NO flash, spark, flame or smoke at any muzzle. The only glow is a tiny ember on the coiled slow-match at the lock beside the shooter's hand, near the stock, with at most a thin thread of smoke rising from that cord. Second, Nagoji gestures back the way they came. He twists slightly at the waist and raises his left hand beside and a little behind his left shoulder, open-handed, with his thumb and fingers pointing back over his shoulder down the road toward the column behind him. His face stays turned toward the raja, and he does not point sideways at the slope. Any mark on his inner left forearm stays a faint, pale, healed patch.

decisions.issues: Clean and on script. The wide high-ridge view shows thick black smoke columns over torched pepper gardens and support poles along a canal. Raiders in plain earth-brown and cream cloth with indigo head cloths walk away unhurried down a scrub path at right. There are no bodies, no red cloth, no muskets or blue coats, and no painted text. The smoke-dimmed grey sky across the top band, especially the paler haze at upper left and centre, holds all three captions. Two minor points: the raiders wear plain shirts rather than going bare-chested, and the two nearest are somewhat close to the ridge rather than far below, but both still read as small, distant figures.

Clean. v02 breaks the bible and its neighbours in three ways. (1) Ponnan grips Nagoji's RIGHT wrist and the talwar is in Nagoji's RIGHT hand: the arm comes from the image-left shoulder of a chest-on torso whose cloth lies over the left shoulder. So the brand and scar are on the right forearm, and in 10.4 Ponnan held the LEFT sword wrist. (2) The brand is a dark inked circular seal or emblem, like a tattoo. The white stitched scar runs ACROSS the wrist like a cut, and it crosses a pale lengthwise line to form a cross. The bible asks for a pale puckered patch, not a cross, and a long white scar running along the forearm. (3) The figures swap sides from 10.3 and 10.4: Ponnan is now on the left and Nagoji on the right, which flips the screen direction. Otherwise the faces, costumes, setting and balloon space were good.

Clean; the round-1 three-hand error is fixed. v02 (only listed candidate) fixes everything the r1 correction asked for: the silver chain of office is on his chest, Padmini has a shawl again, and the brand is now only a pale scar line and patch on the inner LEFT forearm, with no glyph. The staging is also good. Padmini steps in from the dark doorway on her long stick, Nagoji sits cross-legged on the mat listening, and the clay lamp on its stool and the brass basin of faintly pink water sit between them. The large plain laterite wall at upper centre leaves room for both balloons, and the hands and feet are sound. It still fails Nagoji's chapter 23 lock. At 3x zoom his hair is entirely black with brownish highlights and shows no first grey at the temples. The bible row and the MUST MATCH line require that grey, and the neighbouring panels 14.1, 14.2 and 14.5 all show a clear grey streak at the temple, so he would read as the younger, pre-Ananthan Pillai Nagoji for two panels in the middle of the page. A secondary continuity problem: Padmini's shawl is a mid-brown wool, but in 14.2 it is a pale oatmeal, cream-beige fringed shawl. Light stubble shading on his jaw still reads as clean-shaven.
decisions.correction: Keep this v02 composition exactly: Padmini stepping in through the dark timber doorway at left, leaning forward on her long walking stick and frowning toward Nagoji; Nagoji seated cross-legged on the woven mat at right, looking up at her; the clay open-wick lamp on its small stool and the brass basin of faintly pink water on its low stand between them; the plain laterite wall filling the upper centre; his silver chain of office on his bare chest; the brand as only a pale puckered patch beside the long thin white scar on his inner LEFT forearm, with no symbol. Fixes: Nagoji's black topknot hair has a clearly visible streak of first grey at the temple and above the ear on the side facing us, the same grey streak he has in the previous panel, so he reads as the older Ananthan Pillai and not the young Nagoji; keep the rest of his hair black. His chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble texture. Padmini's shawl is the same pale oatmeal, cream-beige woollen shawl with a fringed edge that she wears in the previous panel, loosened around her shoulders over the cream gold-bordered sari, not brown or dark wool.

decisions.issues: v02 (only listed candidate) delivers the beat and the r1 fixes. Padmini leans in close with her hand cupped beside her mouth, whispering, her long stick upright in her other hand and grey threading in her coiled black hair. Nagoji sits in profile turned to her, listening. The silver chain is on his chest, the brand on his inner LEFT forearm is a pale puckered patch beside the long white scar with no glyph, and the clay lamp now sits on a stool between them. There is no painted text and the hands are sound. It fails Nagoji's lock on three points. (1) His hair is all black with no first grey at the temple, against the ch23 bible row and MUST MATCH line and against 14.1, 14.2 and 14.5, which show the grey clearly. In this close two-shot the change is obvious. (2) His chin and whole jaw carry a dotted stubble texture, heavier than the faint shading usually accepted as clean-shaven. (3) Under the ear stud, a second gold bead shows below the lobe, so it reads as a stud with something hanging under it rather than a single flush stud. Continuity: Padmini's shawl is mid-brown wool where 14.2 has a pale oatmeal, cream-beige fringed shawl. The lettering room is also tight. Only a thin band of wall shows above the heads, plus a small patch at upper left beside the stick.
decisions.correction: Keep this v02 composition: Padmini kneeling close at left, leaning in with her left hand cupped beside her mouth as she whispers, her long walking stick upright in her right hand; Nagoji seated cross-legged at right in profile, turned to her, listening; the clay open-wick lamp on a low wooden stool between them; the brass basin on its stand in the lower left foreground; the doorway at right; his silver chain of office on his bare chest; the brand as only a pale puckered patch beside the long thin white scar on his inner LEFT forearm. Fixes: Nagoji's black topknot hair has a clearly visible streak of first grey at the temple and above the ear on the side facing us, the same grey as in the earlier panels on this page; keep the rest of his hair black and the topknot high on the crown. His chin, jaw and cheeks are smooth and clean-shaven, with no stubble dots or texture. His ear carries one tiny flush gold stud on the front of the lobe and nothing at all below or behind the lobe. Padmini's shawl is the same pale oatmeal, cream-beige woollen shawl with a fringed edge from the previous panels, not brown. Pull the camera back slightly so a band of plain laterite wall about a quarter of the frame height shows above both heads, clear of hair, the stick top and faces, for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji has a faint small reddish mark on his brow (the bible's constant identity says no forehead marks), so a retouch is advisable. He holds a spear among the escort, which is acceptable. Otherwise he is correct: topknot, grey temples, gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, and no turban or sash. Varma's hair is loose with a knot at the back of the crown, not a side knot above the left ear. He correctly has no turban or crest, the pearl drops from his sheet, sandal paste, rings, a white angavastram, and no wound before the attack. Brass lamp stands stand in for most of the belikal stones. The large clear sky at upper left, above the royal party, holds both captions.

Minor only. The escort spearmen wear dark leather cross-belts with brass buckles and have beards, so they differ slightly from the plain white-clad spearmen in 15.1. The chaver is correct: close-cropped hair, no moustache, three ash lines on the brow, a curved gutting knife, and a clean leap over the spear line. Anatomy is sound, with no blood and no text. Clear sky at upper left holds both captions.

Minor only. The small background Nagoji has a white namam mark on his brow (bible: no forehead marks) and a gold bangle, so a retouch is advisable. Otherwise he is correct: topknot, grey temples, gold stud, curled moustache, clean chin, silver chain, white mundu, no turban or sash, and his sword half clear of the scabbard. Varma's hair is in a crown knot rather than a side knot above the left ear. Varma correctly shields the heir with his right arm, leaving his back and LEFT shoulder toward the blade, which comes down from the upper right. The attacker appears only as an arm and torso at the right edge. No wound or blood is drawn, the rings and angavastram are correct, and the setting matches 15.1. Clear sky at upper left, beside the gopuram, holds the caption.

Minor only. Varma's hair knot sits high at the crown and toward the back, not clearly a side knot above his left ear. Nagoji's grey is heavier than 'first grey at the temples'. His gold ear ornament is a small bead close to the lobe rather than a perfectly flush stud. His forearm scar and brand show on the outer face of the crossed left forearm. Everything else is correct. Nagoji has a clean-shaven chin, a thick curled moustache, a topknot, no turban or sash, a silver chain, and he stands by a pillar. Ramayyan is in the doorway with a palm-leaf bundle and stylus, looking uneasy. Varma is bare-chested and bare-headed on a low couch, with physicians binding the back of his LEFT shoulder with green paste and cloth. There is no blood or painted text. The room has a black polished floor, carved timber beams and brass oil lamps. The dark carved ceiling across the top band leaves room for the two captions and both balloons.

Clean. Ramayyan is close and hesitating, with a sideways glance toward screen right, where Varma is off-panel. He matches his sheet: thin sharp features, receding curly hair, plain unbordered white cloth, a palm-leaf bundle and a stylus. His hands are sound. There is no text, the room matches 16.4 (carved timber pillars, black polished floor, brass lamps, a doorway onto the night palms), and there is dark low-detail space in the upper right ceiling and the upper left pillar for the three balloons.

v02 (the only listed candidate) changes the script beat and doubles Nagoji. No physician is drawn. Nagoji himself has both hands on Varma's bandaged shoulder, so Varma's raised palm pushes Nagoji away, not 'the physician's restraining hand', and Nagoji is not simply leaning in. Varma also reads as a second Nagoji: loose long grey curls tied in a high crown topknot, a heavy curled moustache, and none of the markers he carries in panels 17.1, 17.2 and 17.5 (pearl drop earrings, white-and-red namam on the brow). The bible wants black hair in a side knot above his LEFT ear, and he has neither. Next to the real Nagoji (crown topknot, grey temples, curled moustache) the two men are nearly interchangeable. What works and should be kept: the room (black floor, timber pillars, brass lamps), the low couch, the clean bandage on Varma's LEFT shoulder, Ramayyan at the left (bald crown, curly sides, palm-leaf bundle at the waist), and Nagoji's own look (stud, silver chain, clean chin, forearm scar).
decisions.correction: Keep the v02 room, the low couch with the red bolster, the brass lamps, the clean white bandage at the back of Varma's LEFT shoulder, and Ramayyan leaning in at the left with his palm-leaf bundle. Change three things. (1) Add a separate physician: an elderly palace vaidyan with white hair and a white beard, a plain white mundu, no chain, no ear stud. He stands just behind Varma's LEFT shoulder with one hand on the bandage, and that is the hand Varma's open right palm pushes away as he sits up. (2) Nagoji does not touch Varma or the bandage. He stands a step back on the right, bent forward at the waist with his hands on his knees or at his sides, so that he is leaning in and nothing more. He is the only man with a high crown topknot, grey temples, a tiny flush gold ear stud and the silver chain of office. (3) Varma must look like himself from the other panels on this page and never like Nagoji: black hair gathered in a low knot at the back of the head behind his LEFT ear, never a high crown topknot and never loose curls; round pearl drop earrings; the white-and-red Vaishnava namam on his brow; long gold bead necklaces; bare-chested in a cream gold-bordered mundu. Keep the upper wall and ceiling between the heads dark and plain for four speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. Varma's hair is heavily grey and gathered in a low bun behind his head, not black in a side knot above the LEFT ear as the bible asks. This matches how he is drawn in panels 17.1, 17.2 and 17.4, and the namam, pearl drops and gold beads match 17.1. The whispering hand belongs to his bandaged LEFT arm, which is plausible. Otherwise clean: bare-headed, no crown or turban, bandage on the LEFT shoulder with no blood, the black polished floor, timber pillars, brass open-wick lamps, no painted text. The plain ochre wall at top left (between the pillars) and top right (beside the face and over the doorway) leaves room for three medium balloons without covering the face or hand.

Minor only: Varma's couch shows only as an edge with draped cloth at the left, which reads fine as an off-panel king. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch23 row: topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, white mundu with cream shoulder cloth, silver chain, and on the LEFT forearm a pale scar and a small brand patch with no letters. The raised hand is sound with five digits. The upper-left wall is clear for the balloon. The black floor, brass lamps and red-and-wood couch match 18.2 and 18.3.

Minor only: the brow mark is a red-and-white namam, where 18.2 shows a plain white one. A grey-haired physician at the right edge tends the shoulder, which the setting allows. Varma matches his sheet: bare-headed with no turban or crest, hair knotted, pearl drops, gold bead necklaces, bare-chested in a white gold-bordered mundu. He lies back with his jaw set. The bandage is on his LEFT shoulder (the near side, with his head to frame right) and shows only skin-tone gaps and white paste, no red. The upper-middle wall is wide and clear for the long balloon. The red bolsters and black floor match 18.2.
